messages:
sam: Customer CustBravo (support ticket #12345) reports p99 API latency ~600-900ms to our /v1/generate endpoint from eu-west-2 users. Started ~09:30 UTC, persists. They see lots of TLS handshake tails. Can SRE triage?
elaine: oncall here, looking now. any repro curl/traceroute from customer?
sam: pasted what they sent: `curl -w '\ntime_connect: %{time_connect}\ntime_appconnect: %{time_appconnect}\ntime_total: %{time_total}\n' -o /dev/null -s https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate` -> time_appconnect spikes to 0.45-0.8s intermittently.
elaine: thanks. starting with our e2e probes + edge telemetry for eu-west-2. raj will help with routing plane.
raj: pulling edge traces. I see increased cross-AZ hops for a subset of flows from eu-west-2 -> eu-west-1 pop between 09:25-09:50 UTC. TTL changes + sudden AS path detours.
karen: network telemetry: around 09:24 there was a regen of BGP sessions with one transit peer in eu-west-2. Multipath selection briefly favored a path that goes via our us-west backbone (adds latency + extra TLS RTT).
route-bot: synthetic probe summary: prod-probe-eu-west-2 -> api-gateway: p95 210ms (baseline 120ms), p99 820ms (baseline 240ms). Spike window 09:25-09:52.
monitor-bot: alert: api.p95.eu-west-2 > 300ms for 28m.
elaine: can someone share a `traceroute -n` from a probe during spike? need to verify cross-pop hop.
sam: customer supplied traceroute: ```traceroute to api.redwood.example (52.30.10.11), 30 hops max, 60 byte packets
 1 10.0.0.1 0.9 ms 0.8 ms 0.8 ms
 2 100.64.0.5 1.1 ms 1.0 ms 1.0 ms
 3 52.220.8.1 120.4 ms 121.0 ms 120.9 ms
 4 34.120.0.3 312.2 ms 313.1 ms 312.8 ms
 5 52.30.10.11 312.9 ms 313.0 ms 312.7 ms```
raj: hop 3 -> 4 looks like the detour to us-west backbone. that explains the +200ms.
karen: yep, one transit dropped one of the eu-west paths and ECMP collapsed to the longer path for some prefixes. we have a partial peer flap recorded.
elaine: short-term mitigation: can we steer traffic for affected prefixes back to eu-west local transit or pin customers to nearest PoP?
karen: updating GSLB weights now for the impacted CDN prefixes to prefer eu-west-2 PoPs where available. will take ~30s to propagate. also asking transit to re-evaluate BGP metrics.
raj: I can add a temporary route policy to prefer direct eu-west peers for customer IP blocks (custBravo prefix range) until BGP heals. pushing now.
route-bot: action: set route-preference eu-west-2 for prefixes 203.0.113.0/24 -> applied (propagation 12s).
elaine: nice. can we also enable TLS session reuse / keepalive on the gateway for this tenant to reduce handshake frequency?
sam: support: customer uses short-lived clients; enabling session reuse might help but we should confirm client behavior. I'll check with them.
raj: traffic shift visible: our probes show p99 dropping from ~820ms -> ~240ms within 40s of route change.
monitor-bot: resolved alert: api.p95.eu-west-2 back to 150ms.
elaine: great. next steps: 1) keep route policy for 2 hours, 2) follow up with transit provider for root cause of flap, 3) postmortem with network + infra. I'll own the action items.
karen: logged ticket NW-789, flagged for provider SLA review.
sam: I told customer we mitigated and asked them to confirm. they replied: "latency looks normal now, thanks" :thumbsup:.
elaine: assign postmortem, please include time series of TLS handshake time_appconnect, traceroutes, BGP session logs, and any config pushes around 09:20-09:30.
raj: grabbing kernel-level socket logs and edge gateway tcpdump around spike window, will drop in the postmortem doc.
karen: will collect transit BGP logs and community tags.
elaine: thanks all. marking oncall handoff notes and will add to morning all-hands summary. leaving route policy in place for 1h then revert if stable.
route-bot: scheduled revert of temporary route-preference in 1h (2026-03-17T11:10:00Z) unless extended.
elaine: closing thread once postmortem doc is complete.
